key_insight: Hydrograd v2.0 makes unstructured-mesh shallow-water simulations differentiable, enabling efficient parameter calibration and closure learning with steady and unsteady adjoints.
engineering_relevance: It supports hydraulic calibration on meshes from production models such as SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D, including flows with wetting and drying.
method: Python/JAX finite-volume solver with well-balanced, positivity-preserving treatment.
Newton steady solves with graph-coloured sparse Jacobians; implicit gradients require one linear solve.
Unsteady gradients via checkpointed reverse mode or an implicit time integrator.
evidence_signal: Reported tests show steady gradients agreeing with finite differences to about 10⁻⁸, Savannah River water-surface RMSE of 4.7 mm versus SRH-2D, and steady closure learning 96× faster than differentiation through time marching.
watch_item: Spatial roughness calibration is sensitive to gauge placement: recovering all five zone values required gauges in every zone in the reported test.
paper_title: Hydrograd v2.0: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes with steady and unsteady adjoints for calibration and closure learning
